rv.q: This production of Rhinoceros is galvanizing.
Long live Bérenger; long live Ionesco; and long live Diane Paulus and her reign at A.R.T.!
I don’t imagine you’ll see a piece of theater as mind-bendingly funny as the first half of the Theatre’s production of “Rhinoceros” any time soon.
It deserves to be seen by an even larger audience, and here's hoping it makes its way to a New York City stage soon.
Rightly so, it’s a grand production worthy of its hype.
A.R.T.’s production makes that meaning clear without sacrificing the comedy that makes the story so entertaining.
John Turturro's scruffy, strident, and anguished Berenger gives the production its necessary mix of horror, humor, and desperate resistance.

cn.t: Turturro and Giamatti lead a stellar cast in Paulus's timely revival that's hilarious in its first half, chilling in its second. Critics praise the absurdist classic's prescient take on conformity, though dialogue-heavy stretches occasionally drag.
